messages:
emily.docs: Flagging PR #2733 1: mismatch in the pagination examples for /v1/embeds/list. Docs show `cursor` as an integer offset (e.g. 100) while runtime expects an opaque string cursor token. Customers who copy the example into curl get a 400.

emily.docs: Example in the PR: `GET /v1/embeds/list?limit=50&cursor=100` -> runtime returns 400: {"error":"invalid cursor format"}.

nikhil-api: Ah yeah, we switched to opaque continuation tokens last quarter to support keyset-style paging. OpenAPI schema has `cursor: string` but one of the rendered examples was accidentally updated to show an offset. Good catch.

nikhil-api: Runtime accepts tokens like `cTkn:1:eyJ...` (base64 payload). We prefer not to publish internal structure but we should show a realistic placeholder.

sara-sdk: This caused the Go/Java SDK integration tests to fail because our generated pagination example helper used the docs example as the baseline. The helper tries to append numeric offsets and then fails server validation. JS/py ignored it but typed clients failed.

emily.docs: Proposed doc fix: update examples to use `cursor=eyJjdHgiOiIxMjM0...` (shortened token), add a one-line sentence: "cursor is an opaque continuation token returned by prior list calls; do not treat it as a numeric offset." Also add a short note about how to iterate pages safely with code snippets for Python and Go.

sara-sdk: For SDKs, I'll add a Paginate helper that takes the last cursor string and repeatedly calls list until cursor=="" or null. Also add a typed wrapper in Go that treats cursor as string and documents that callers shouldn't parse it. I'll open PR with tests. ETA: 4h.

ci-bot: CI: docs PR #2733 lint OK; integration tests failing: pagination/ListCursorTypeTest. See https://ci.internal/rdw/2733/job/42.

deploy-bot: @here deploy scheduled: docs staging site refresh at 18:00 UTC. Hold off merging until SDK PR lands unless we're only changing examples.

nikhil-api: Action plan: 1) I'll patch the OpenAPI canonical examples to replace numeric offset with a plausible opaque token and add the schema description clarifying it's opaque. 2) @emily.docs will update the API ref, add both a short curl loop and a Go snippet showing use of the new Paginate helper. 3) @sara-sdk will push the SDK PR with helper + tests. 4) We'll coordinate a rolling merge: OpenAPI -> SDK -> Docs, and then push staging refresh. Target: tomorrow morning.

emily.docs: Adding a small troubleshooting FAQ: "400 on embeds.list? Check cursor format / ensure you're using continuation token." I'll link to the SDK helper in the example.

sara-sdk: Note for reviewers: helper will accept both empty string and nil cursor; it will stop when server cursor is empty. It will also surface server-provided rate-limit headers so callers can implement backoff.

nikhil-api: Thanks. Quick follow-up: avoid revealing sample token structure. Use a short opaque placeholder like `cursor=ctok_ABC123` in public docs.

emily.docs: Good call 44d I'll use `ctok_ABC123` in public docs and include a snippet showing retrieval from the previous response: `cursor = response.meta.next_cursor` so customers see the flow.

ci-bot: Reminder: run the pagination smoke test after merge (test harness: tests/pagination_smoke.py).

emily.docs: will do post-merge smoke with staging. Thanks all!
